sea_level_note: Chosen from the data: 10th percentile of the lidar DEM on the first 4 m of land at the NAIP waterline, so the imaged wet-sand swash band sits just above the water. ~1 m above Coos Bay MSL (~1.0 m NAVD88), i.e. about mean higher high water, matching the tide + wave run-up in both the lidar and the NAIP scene.

lake_id_file.meaning: 0 = no lake water; k = water surface (open water or flooded marsh) of the lake with id k (lakes[k-1]).

water_rendering: Ocean: one unbounded plane at sea_level_m (all land is >= sea_level_m + 0.03, all ocean cells are below it). Lakes: one flat polygon per lake at level_m built from lakes[].polygons_xz (outer rings, islands filled in: island terrain is above the level and pokes through). Do NOT clip lake planes by bbox_m only: terrain inside some bboxes lies below that lake's level (e.g. the western deflation plain at 5.8-6.5 m). Alternative: mask a plane with lake_id.u8.
trails_note: Centre-lines (world x,z in m) of the traced trails; cells within ~1.5 m are habitat ROAD_TRAIL.

colormap.note: NAIP true colour resampled onto exactly the DEM extent (UV 0..1 == world extent, v=0 at the north edge)

sources.vegetation_targets: Eriksson et al. 2019 PLOS ONE 14(5):e0214653, Fig. 6

manual_features.note: cabin / outbuilding east of the lake causeway

notes: Grid = the DEM grid as delivered by the 3DEP service: square cells of 2.756552 Web-Mercator m = 2.00055 ground m (scale k = cos(lat0) = 0.725744). The service widened the requested x-extent by 1.059 merc-m on each side; NAIP was resampled with its own georeferencing onto this grid. Ocean: NAIP water + surf connected to the west edge; synthetic seabed sea_level - (0.4 + 0.035 d) clamped >= -8 m, joined to the beach by a cubic ramp over the first 10 m. Lakes: hydro-flattened DEM areas that are water in NAIP (level = flattened elevation) plus small ponds detected in NAIP and checked against DEM depressions; beds carved to level - min(2.5, 0.12 d + 0.15). Vegetated cells inside the flattened areas are flooded emergent marsh (habitat MARSH, terrain 0.25 m below the level) and belong to the lake's water surface (lake_id, polygons_xz); area_m2 = water surface, open_water_m2 = open water only. All other land within 40 m of water is >= level + 0.08 m. Water depth = level_m - terrain height. Several lakes share almost the same level (7.03-7.05 m), so mask water by lake_id / polygons, not by bbox.
